extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, institutional grants administrators, PDs/PIs, and recipients managing NIH grants (especially those preparing modular budgets, conference (R13/U13) applications, or consortium/subaward agreements).
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation/administrative requirements from the NIH Grants Policy Statement covering modular budgets, support of scientific meetings (R13/U13), allowable/unallowable costs, required safety plans, reporting/closeout, and consortium agreement requirements for applicants and recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular budget justification and year-to-year variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative budget justification is required if there is a variation in the number of modules requested from year to year; requests for adjustments to reflect substantial changes in expected future activities may be requested at the outset (e.g., major equipment purchase may justify higher budget in that year). There is no provision for escalation in future years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When pre-award review warrants it, NIH ICs may request a detailed budget as part of the Just-in-Time process. Use narrative justification to explain year-specific changes; do not assume automatic escalation across future years.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRG evaluation of budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) evaluate the budget based on a general, expert estimate of the total effort and resources required to carry out the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If SRG recommends adjustment, it will be in terms of an entire module. Applicants should propose modular budgets consistent with anticipated effort and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC pre-award information requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Following peer review, for applications being considered for award, the IC will request information about 'Other Support' and, as applicable, the use of human subjects or vertebrate animals, and education in the protection of human research participants. Additional budget information will be requested before award only under special circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to supply Other Support, human/animal use documentation, and educational certifications as part of Just-in-Time materials if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount determination and cost management
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will attempt to make awards at or close to the level of total direct costs recommended by the SRG, taking other support into account; an IC may need to reduce the award amount to accommodate the IC’s cost management plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should not assume the SRG-recommended amount is guaranteed; IC fiscal constraints may reduce awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award budget form for modular awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The award budget will be a noncategorical budget specifying approved total direct costs and indirect costs, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modular awards are issued without detailed direct cost categories; recipients must track costs per applicable cost principles and NIHGPS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award allocation obligations for modular awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion in allocating and accounting for costs related to modular awards within their organizational accounting system, but must ensure all costs charged are in accordance with applicable cost principles, the NIHGPS, and any legislatively imposed restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain internal accounting practices that document compliance with federal cost principles despite the noncategorical award format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebudgeting provision for modular grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the award is issued without direct cost budget categories, the significant rebudgeting provision described as a potential change of scope indicator does not apply to modular grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should still follow other prior approval rules as applicable, but the specific significant rebudgeting provision is not applicable for modular awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative supplements require non-modular budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may submit requests for administrative supplements to the CGMO of the NIH awarding IC, but must provide a detailed (non-modular) budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking administrative supplements, prepare a full categorical budget even if the underlying award is modular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing Revisions submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing Revisions should be submitted to NIH using the modular budget component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow modular budget format for Competing Revisions submissions per instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH support for conferences (general eligibility and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports scientific meetings, conferences, and workshops relevant to its mission under R13 and U13 activity codes. Support is contingent on IC interests and priorities. Applications must be submitted based on published receipt dates. Generally, NIH will not issue a conference grant unless the Federal award date can precede the conference start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check IC-specific budget guidelines and highlighted topics before submission; awards after the conference are allowed only when IC documents funding of post-conference activities consistent with the approved application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: Conference and meeting types
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference: event whose primary purpose is to disseminate technical information beyond the recipient/subrecipient (2 CFR 200.432). Scientific meeting: gathering to coordinate, exchange, disseminate info or explore/clarify a defined subject. International conference: designated by sponsor or open invitations to participants in two or more countries other than US/Canada. Domestic conference: held in US or Canada primarily for U.S. or U.S.-Canadian participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurately classify your meeting (domestic vs international) to determine eligibility and allowable support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic institutions/organizations, including scientific/professional societies, are eligible. International conferences may be supported only through the U.S. representative organization of an established international society. Individuals are not eligible to receive a grant in support of a conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If organizing an international meeting, apply through an eligible U.S. organizational sponsor; do not submit as an individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference application submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are electronically submitted using an application package combining SF424 (R&R) and PHS398 components. Applicants must complete and submit a detailed categorical budget using the Research & Related Budget component; however, no indirect costs may be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the NOFO and IC contacts for any IC-specific budget or project duration requirements; do not include indirect costs in the budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hotel and Motel Fire Safety Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Federally funded meetings and conferences cannot be held in properties that do not comply with PL101-391: hard-wired single-station smoke detectors in each guestroom (NFPA 72) and an automatic sprinkler system with a sprinkler head in each guest room (NFPA 13 or 13R), except properties three stories or lower are exempt from sprinkler requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the National Master List maintained by USFA; select compliant venues to avoid ineligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required conference safety plan elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference organizers of NIH-supported meetings must provide a 'safety plan' (as part of JIT) that will be communicated to attendees. Safety plans are required to include: statement of commitment to a safe environment; expectations of behavior (including list of behaviors considered harassing, with emphasis on sexual, racial, ethnic harassment); instructions for confidential reporting; description of how organizers will assess allegations and consequences for violations; information on contacting HHS OCR and how to file complaints; information that filing with organizer is not required before filing with OCR; information on notifying NIH about harassment concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants recommended for funding must also provide a description of the strategy to communicate the Safety Plan, a plan to document allegations and resulting actions, and steps organizers will take to ensure a safe environment. NIH staff will review and must approve Safety Plans prior to award; incomplete/unsatisfactory plans must be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference application review criteria (programmatic relevance and personnel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be reviewed for programmatic relevance and merit. Reviewers will evaluate PD(s)/PI(s) Personal Statement of the Biographical Sketch: Are PD(s)/PI(s) well suited for organizing and fulfilling conference goals? Are qualifications and past performance appropriate? Are key personnel and selected speakers appropriate and well suited for their roles?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize PD/PI experience in organizing meetings, list appropriate key personnel and speaker qualifications, and document past performance where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding mechanisms and constraints for conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants or cooperative agreements may be used. Cooperative agreements may be used if NIH needs substantial involvement. Grant funds may not be used for general support of international conferences held in the US/Canada; only specific aspects (e.g., a symposium or workshop) may be funded. Awards for a single conference usually have a project period of 1 year. Permanently sponsoring organizations may receive up to 5 years funding annually contingent on availability and satisfactory progress. Change in focus requires prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project periods and scopes accordingly; document intended use of funds for specific aspects when supporting international meetings in US/Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment/disclaimer and logo use requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must include specified funding acknowledgment/disclaimer on conference materials. Use of NIH or HHS logos requires prior approval; unauthorized use may result in civil monetary penalties (42 CFR Part 1003).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the exact language provided in the policy on promotional materials, agendas, and websites. Seek prior approval before using government logos.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principle for allowable conference costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with 2 CFR Part 200.432, conference hosts/sponsors must ensure conference costs are appropriate, necessary, and managed to minimize Federal costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document necessity and reasonableness of requested conference costs in the application and budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost: Conference services
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds may be used for necessary recording of proceedings, simultaneous translation, and subsequent transcriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these items in the categorical budget with explanation of their necessity to conference objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost: Consultant services
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds may be used to pay consultant fees, including travel and supporting costs (per diem or, where applicable, subsistence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify consultant roles and include consultant costs in the detailed budget; follow recipient policies for consultant payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost: Equipment rental
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds may be used for the rental of necessary equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate rental vs purchase; purchases are unallowable under conference grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost: Meals (working meals)
rubrics_metrics.description: When meals are justified by the applicant as an integral and necessary part of a conference (i.e., a working meal where business is transacted), grant funds may be used, provided that meal costs are not duplicated in participants’ per diem or subsistence allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the meal is integral; avoid duplicative reimbursement and reflect adjustments where meals are included in registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost: Publication costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds may be used to pay for entire or partial cost of publication of proceedings or materials (special plates, charts, diagrams, printing, distribution, mailing, postage, handling) unless otherwise specified at award time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget publication costs when dissemination of proceedings is a project objective; account for potential program income if materials sold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost: Registration fees limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds may not be used for registration fees paid by the recipient to other organizations on behalf of attendees. Grant funds may be used to help defray registration costs for some select conference attendees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not budget to pay third-party registration fees for attendees; describe criteria for selecting attendees whose registration might be defrayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost: Salaries and staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds may be used for all or part of salaries of professional personnel, clerical assistants, editorial assistants, and other non-professional staff in proportion to the time or effort directly related to the conference, in accordance with recipient policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document effort allocation and comply with recipient salary policies; keep supporting time-and-effort records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost: Speakers' fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Speakers’ fees for services rendered are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include speaker fees in the budget and justify as necessary to achieve conference goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost: Supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds may be used for purchase of supplies for the conference if supplies are received and used during the budget period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit supplies to items directly supporting the conference and within the budget period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost: Travel rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may be used for travel of staff, speakers, participants, and attendees if identified in the application and approved at time of award. Travel expenses for recipient employees governed by recipient travel policies applied consistently. U.S. foreign travel restrictions in effect at award time will be followed. Transportation costs may not exceed coach class. Where possible, U.S. flag carriers will be used. Proposed per diem/subsistence must be reasonable and limited to days of attendance plus actual travel time. Local mileage only may be paid for local participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List travelers and justify travel in application. Ensure travel and per diem amounts follow recipient policies and federal restrictions; document use of U.S. flag carriers where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable temporary dependent care costs during travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 2 CFR Part 200.475, temporary dependent care costs above regular dependent care that directly result from travel to conferences are allowable provided: (1) costs are direct result of individual's travel for the Federal award; (2) costs consistent with recipient/subrecipient's documented travel policy for all entity travel; (3) costs are temporary during the travel period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure dependent care reimbursement follows recipient policy and is limited to the travel period; travel costs for dependents are unallowable except for travel of six months or more with prior HHS approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unallowable conference costs (list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unallowable costs include: A&R (not allowable); entertainment and personal expenses (amusement, diversion, social activities, ceremonials, bar charges, tips, personal telephone calls, laundry charges); equipment purchase; indirect costs; honoraria given for conferring distinction; local participants’ expenses (except local mileage); membership dues; research patient care; visas and passports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not request or expend grant funds for these items; describe any borderline items (e.g., meals vs social events) with clear justification to avoid disallowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property, publications, copyright, and public disclosure for conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recipient publishes material developed in whole or in part with NIH funds, the material may be distributed free. If sold, proceeds are program income and must be accounted for. Recipients are free to arrange for copyright, but any copyrighted publication is subject to a nonexclusive, irrevocable, royalty-free right to the Federal agency to reproduce/publish/use the work for Federal purposes and to authorize others. Presentations/discussions constitute public disclosure and could impact IP rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for sales proceeds as program income on the FFR. Warn participants about public disclosure risks to intellectual property; report inventions to the recipient per NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference reporting and record retention requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion/termination of a conference grant, recipients must submit the final RPPR and final FFR in accordance with Closeout provisions. Records of expenditures and any program income must be maintained per 2 CFR Part 200.328.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare final RPPR and FFR; retain supporting documents and financial records for audit and closeout review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report contents and timelines for conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: For single conferences, a final report must be submitted electronically or by paper within 120 days after the end of the project period. The report must include: grant number; title, date, place; name(s) of conference director/PD/PIs; organization name; list of individuals and affiliations who participated as speakers/discussants in formally planned sessions; a summary of topics discussed/conclusions. For multi-year awards, an annual progress report is required at least 6 months before the next scheduled conference; final progress report within 120 days after project period end. Proceedings/publications may substitute for final report if they contain required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect speaker lists, agendas, and summaries during the conference to facilitate timely reporting; plan annual progress reports for recurring conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Federal Financial Report (FFR) submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submission of the final FFR through PMS is required within 120 days after the end of the project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with institutional financial offices to ensure timely FFR submission and retention of expenditure records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium agreement overarching responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Under consortium agreements, the recipient is the direct and primary recipient of NIH funds and is accountable to NIH for project performance, appropriate expenditure of funds by all parties, reporting requirements, and other obligations; terms and conditions flow down to subrecipients in accordance with 2 CFR Part 200.101(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must actively manage and oversee consortium participants to ensure compliance and fulfillment of NIH obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAM.gov debarment/suspension check for potential subrecipients
rubrics_metrics.description: The direct recipient must confirm in SAM.gov that a potential subrecipient is not suspended, debarred, or otherwise excluded from receiving Federal funds (see 2 CFR Part 180.300).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform and document SAM.gov checks for each subrecipient before awarding subawards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarding to a single recipient and PD/PI listing
rubrics_metrics.description: The award will be made to a single recipient with a single PD/PI even though one or more organizations will carry out portions of the activity. With multiple PD/PI model, all PD/PIs are listed on the award regardless of affiliation, with the Contact PD/PI so noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure applications to identify the Contact PD/PI and list other PD/PIs appropriately per the multiple PD/PI guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass-through entity substantive role requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The pass-through entity must perform a substantive role in conduct of the planned research and not merely serve as a conduit of funds; must provide appropriate oversight of scientific, programmatic, financial, and administrative matters related to the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the substantive activities and oversight plans of the pass-through entity in the application and consortium agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient certification requirements (2 CFR Part 200.415(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subrecipients (at all tiers) must provide the pass-through entity with a certification statement as outlined in 2 CFR Part 200.415(b) whenever applying for funds, requesting payment, and submitting financial reports. The certification must be maintained pursuant to 2 CFR 200.334.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect, retain, and produce subordinate certification statements as part of subaward files and financial reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirements for consortium arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must include all proposed performance sites (applicant organization and consortium participants). Non-modular grant applications must include complete detailed budgets for each consortium participant. Modular grant applications must include an estimate of consortium total costs (direct + indirect) each year as part of the budget narrative justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare detailed budget pages for each subrecipient in non-modular applications; for modulars, include clear consortium cost estimates in the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium site lead investigator designation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For each consortium site it is appropriate and expected that someone be designated as the consortium lead investigator responsible for ensuring proper conduct of the project at the consortium site. This individual must be assigned the PD/PI role only when a multiple PD/PI application is being submitted; otherwise assign another project role in Senior/Key Personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign roles consistent with the application type and document responsibilities for the consortium lead investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: AOR/SO signature attestation regarding consortium agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature (or electronic equivalent) of the Authorized Organization Representative/Signing Official (AOR/SO) on the application signifies that the applicant organization and all proposed consortium participants understand and agree that programmatic and administrative personnel are aware of NIH consortium agreement policy and prepared to establish required inter-organizational agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional officials and consortium participants review and accept consortium policies prior to application submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH may request additional consortium information and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may request additional information before award and may place specific award condition(s) on the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to respond to NIH requests and accept award conditions; failure to provide requested documentation may lead to remedies for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written agreement minimum required contents for consortium participants
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must enter into a formal written agreement with each consortium participant/subrecipient addressing negotiated arrangements for meeting scientific, administrative, financial, and reporting requirements and ensuring compliance with Federal regulations. At a minimum the agreement must include identification of consortium lead investigator and roles/responsibilities; procedures for directing/monitoring research; reimbursement procedures (dollar ceiling, method/schedule, supporting documentation, review/approval procedures, timing of reports), access to core facilities and fee-for-service terms; determination of travel/salary/fringe benefit policies if different; terms establishing which Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI) policy applies; certifications or time periods for FCOI disclosure reporting to enable timely PHS reporting; provision addressing ownership/disposition of data (including whether resources will be freely available); requirement to apply NIH data sharing and inventions/patent policy and to report inventions to the recipient; expectations for authorship; provisions re property, program income, publications, reporting, and audit; provisions regarding UEI and subrecipient reporting under FFATA (recipient must provide FAIN to subrecipients); incorporation of applicable public policy requirements and intent to comply; outline all required certifications in 2 CFR Part 200.415; provision for immediate termination of subaward if subrecipient is suspended/debarred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this bulleted list as a checklist when drafting subaward agreements. If a subrecipient is unwilling to sign, do not issue a subaward. Retain copies of agreements and supporting documentation for NIH oversight and audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium public policy and human subjects/animal welfare responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient must determine whether a consortium participant has filed assurances with NIH covering its activities and, if not, ensure required assurances/certifications are submitted. Recipient responsible for ensuring all sites engaged in human subjects research have appropriate OHRP-approved assurances and IRB approval consistent with 45 CFR Part 46. Animal welfare requirements that apply to recipients also apply to consortium participants; recipient must ensure performance sites have approved Animal Welfare Assurance and valid IACUC approval. If pass-through entity lacks an approved Assurance and animal work will be done at an institution with an Assurance, recipient must obtain an Inter-institutional Assurance from OLAW. Recipient is responsible for complying with NIH prior approval requirements related to adding sites not included in the approved application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify and document Assurances/IRB/IACUC approvals prior to relying on consortium participants for human or animal research; obtain Inter-institutional Assurance when needed and follow prior approval procedures for adding sites.
